cover.alt: Winding World cover art — Gyroid facing Count Null
cover.prompt: Using Gyroid and Count Null character refs as anchors: wide cinematic key art, no text — Gyroid and Count Null face off; looped causeway, stitched spheres, covering sheets; violet collapse vs amber repairs; painterly stylized 3D; teal–amber–violet.

story.title: Winding World
story.premise: The Winding World is a living landscape of looped causeways, stitched surfaces, and towers whose rooms unfold into higher dimensions. When Count Null activates the Null Crown, he promises to simplify every province into a perfect point, but his machinery destroys essential holes and gluing data rather than preserving their shape. Gyroid, a surface-born courier carrying an anchor spool, escapes the first collapse and joins engineer Emmy Boundary to reconnect the world's severed routes. To reach the Crown, Gyroid must outmaneuver Null's enforcer, the Commutator, follow paths through hidden covering sheets, rebuild cycles and their dual signals, and recover the twists that hold the world's upper tower together. Every repair is a construction or obstruction the player can demonstrate: the final victory restores the world's compatible connections without erasing the differences that make its provinces distinct.
story.tone: Wonder-filled mathematical adventure; tactile, luminous, gently punning, with threatening geometric machinery and hopeful reconstruction.
story.teaching_spine: Five worlds follow Hatcher's five chapters, one key concept per level. Each world opens with Count Null exploiting what the player's current tool cannot see — a ring 'is' a point (World 0), the sphere 'is' a point because loops shrink (World 1), the torus 'is' S¹∨S¹∨S² because homology matches (World 2), S³ → S² 'must' be trivial (World 3), homotopy groups 'are' the whole space (World 4) — and the next world's invariant refutes him.

locations.name: Retract Reef
locations.description: Turquoise thickened graph walkways over a luminous sea. Amber spines remain fixed as their neighborhoods retract; cylinder workshops let players extend boundary motions continuously.

locations.name: Skeleton Foundry
locations.description: An open industrial valley of vertex furnaces, oriented edge cranes and disk presses. A torus gate displays its attaching polygon and glued form side by side; the approach network has a marked collapsible spanning tree.

locations.name: Bouquet Bastion
locations.description: Two unfilled loop districts meet at a single beacon. Red and violet causeways keep travel order visible; thickened open neighborhoods provide the connected overlap for the van Kampen construction.

locations.name: Sheetwater Viaduct
locations.description: A connected three-sheet cover of the bouquet, shown as layered glass routes with locally matched labeled ports. Sheet changes occur only by traversing lifted edges, never by jumping between visual layers.

locations.name: Chain Delta
locations.description: An annular wetland built from oriented triangular platforms, with a conspicuously absent central region. Signed face projections reveal interior-edge cancellation while the missing center preserves a nonbounding cycle.

locations.name: Degree Dynamo
locations.description: A spherical power station with overlapping polar maintenance patches and an equatorial belt. Map projectors show signed sphere wraps; a transparent ball chamber exposes the false boundary retractor's induced-map contradiction.

locations.name: Cup Product Gardens
locations.description: A toroidal signal garden beside a counterfeit wedge of two circles and a sphere. Ordered triangulations and cochain sensors let players distinguish the stations by cup products rather than silhouettes or homology groups alone.

locations.name: Poincaré Reach
locations.description: A closed toroidal province with primal and dual route networks, and a separate projective-plane annex displayed through a disk with antipodal boundary identifications. Orientation transport and coefficient switching reveal different fundamental-class rules.

locations.name: Freudenthal Ascent
locations.description: A vertical series of double-cone lifts and based-cube projection chambers. Dimension and connectivity controls expose suspension's valid range; higher-dimensional spaces are represented by manipulable finite diagrams and slices.

locations.name: Postnikov Spire
locations.description: Count Null's fortress of linked stages suspended above the provinces. Two authored simply connected Postnikov-stage consoles display finite cochain models, k-invariant couplings and obstruction witnesses; restored lifts lead to the Crown's collapse engine.

characters.name: Gyroid
characters.description: A curious surface-born courier whose sea-glass armor has the saddle-shaped passages of a gyroid minimal surface. Uses anchored deformations and constructive proofs rather than destructive force. Learns alongside the player; failed moves reveal a concrete continuity, boundary, or obstruction witness.
characters.image_prompt: Game-ready full-body hero portrait of Gyroid, an agile androgynous surface-born courier, sculptural teal sea-glass armor with flowing gyroid minimal-surface saddle passages and rounded perforations, warm amber face visor, coral scarf, brass anchor spool at hip trailing a luminous loop, hopeful adventurous pose. Painterly high-end stylized 3D fantasy, readable silhouette, midnight blue simple background, soft rim light. No text, letters, interface or watermark.

characters.name: Emmy Boundary
characters.description: A practical engineer with stitched triangular workwear and a portable cell forge. Offers manipulable examples and hypothesis checks instead of answers; her evolving workshop converts chains into cochain sensors.
characters.image_prompt: Game-ready full-body portrait of Emmy Boundary, warm older woman engineer with dark skin and silver coiled hair, amber goggles, indigo patchwork coat assembled from triangular panels with copper seams, tool belt, holding a floating luminous triangular cell in articulated brass gloves. Confident friendly pose, painterly stylized 3D fantasy, midnight blue plain background, teal and amber lighting. No text, letters, interface or watermark.

characters.name: The Commutator
characters.description: Count Null's theatrical route marshal, wearing two loop-shaped pauldrons and wielding ordered ribbon patrols. His first encounter exposes noncommuting routes; his final counterfeit station is defeated by a nonzero cup product, showing that matching homology groups do not guarantee matching topology.
characters.image_prompt: Full-body game boss portrait, The Commutator, elegant geometric armored marshal with two enormous asymmetrical loop pauldrons, one red copper one violet steel, four ordered ribbon trails sweeping around a narrow black mask, angular boots, theatrical fencing stance, menacing but whimsical mathematical fantasy. Strong readable silhouette, painterly stylized 3D, midnight blue background, crimson and violet rim lighting. No text, letters, interface or watermark.

characters.name: Count Null
characters.description: An austere sovereign who mistakes erasing structure for simplifying it. His collapse machinery can physically destroy holes but cannot make the resulting maps homotopy equivalences. Challenges the hero with false retractions, overextended theorems, and missing tower couplings; defeated by restored constructions and explicit obstruction witnesses.
characters.image_prompt: Full-body main villain portrait of Count Null, tall austere geometric sovereign in layered obsidian robes converging toward a tiny dark orb, pale porcelain mask, floating broken circular crown of black metal with violet inward-pointing prongs, luminous torn surface fragments orbiting one gloved hand. Regal threatening mathematical fantasy, distinct silhouette, painterly stylized 3D, plain midnight background, violet rim light with amber accents. No text, letters, interface or watermark.

assets.name: Homotopy Anchor Spool
assets.description: Gyroid's brass reel pins designated subspaces and basepoints while the player drags a continuous deformation. Ghost trails show the full motion, not just endpoints; invalid moves highlight the first broken constraint. Later anchors cube boundaries and tower access maps.
assets.image_prompt: Isolated game item icon of an intricate brass spool with teal glass core, luminous turquoise thread forming a flexible closed loop and three amber anchor pins, tactile mathematical fantasy tool, stylized painterly 3D, readable silhouette, dark navy background, no text or UI.

assets.name: CW Cell-Smith
assets.description: A portable forge that builds vertices, oriented edges and disks with selectable boundary attachments. Preview the attaching map before committing; quotient and cone settings are explicitly different from homotopy-preserving collapse tools.
assets.image_prompt: Isolated game item render of a portable brass and indigo geometric forge gauntlet, levitating a point bead, curved edge and translucent triangular disk above its palm, luminous amber attachment seams, stylized painterly 3D, navy background, no text or UI.

assets.name: Van Kampen Clasp
assets.description: Joins route records at a shared basepoint and keeps generator order visible as colored beads. Adjacent inverse pairs snap away; rearranging unlike generators is forbidden unless an installed relation justifies it.
assets.image_prompt: Isolated fantasy puzzle tool, two copper clasp jaws joining red and violet loop cords at one brilliant amber bead, ordered colored beads along cords, finely crafted brass, stylized painterly 3D inventory icon, navy background, no text or UI.

assets.name: Deckhand's Sheet Compass
assets.description: Tracks a path's current sheet and projects its unique lift from a chosen starting vertex. Local ports reveal invalid covering edges; its needle never allows arbitrary sheet switching.
assets.image_prompt: Isolated magical compass with three stacked translucent glass disks, tiny connected luminous route bridges between layers, brass rim and coral needle, teal amber violet palette, stylized painterly 3D inventory icon on navy background, no text or UI.

assets.name: Boundary Blade ∂
assets.description: A non-destructive geometric blade that extracts the signed boundary of a selected chain. Oppositely oriented shared faces cancel in its projection; applying it twice leaves zero. Repairs chains and dismantles false boundary shields without cutting the underlying space.
assets.image_prompt: Isolated hero weapon icon, elegant brass hilt with a hollow triangular energy blade, three luminous oriented edge ribbons surrounding an empty translucent center, teal and amber light, mathematical fantasy, painterly stylized 3D, dark navy background, no writing symbols or UI.

assets.name: Cup-and-Cap Caster
assets.description: Twin-channel cochain gauntlet evaluates front and back simplex faces to form cup products; its cap mode turns cocycles and a chosen fundamental cycle into dual routes. Requires declared coefficients and exposes coboundary errors instead of granting arbitrary magic.
assets.image_prompt: Isolated fantasy gauntlet weapon with twin cup-shaped copper emitters, teal and coral light streams meeting over a floating triangular crystal, layered indigo bracer, precise geometric filigree, painterly stylized 3D inventory render, navy background, no text or UI.

assets.name: Freudenthal Suspension Sling
assets.description: Projects a space between two cone tips and transports sphere-map probes under suspension. A hypothesis latch checks connectivity and probe dimension before promising an isomorphism; boundary-range probes receive only a surjection guarantee.
assets.image_prompt: Isolated mathematical fantasy tool shaped as an elegant brass sling, two opposed glowing cone tips enclosing a suspended teal sphere, curved indigo handle with amber joints, crisp silhouette, painterly stylized 3D on dark navy background, no text or UI.

assets.name: Null Crown
assets.description: Count Null's destructive collapse engine, a crown coupled to the tower. It erases geometric structure rather than proving homotopy equivalence. In the finale the player disconnects its drive after repairing the missing stage couplings, preserving the reconstructed world.
assets.image_prompt: Isolated final boss artifact, floating broken obsidian crown with inward violet prongs surrounding a tiny dark orb, torn luminous geometric surface fragments caught at its rim, ominous yet elegant stylized painterly 3D, dark navy backdrop, no text or UI.

meta.structure_revision: 2026-10-16: chapter = world, key concept = level (replaces 10-level plan)

worlds.title: Retract Reef
worlds.theme: Thick walkways over a luminous sea, built and rebuilt cell by cell. What does it mean for two shapes to be 'the same'?

null_claim.claim: A ring is just a point that hasn't been simplified yet.
null_claim.why_it_works_here: World 0 can show deformations that work, but has no invariant that proves one is impossible (Hatcher p. 3 defers this to Chapter 1).

levels.title: A Good Deformation
levels.concept: Deformation retraction: shrink X onto a subspace A by sliding points, with f₀ = identity, f₁(X) = A, A fixed throughout, and continuity in both point and time.
levels.goal: Save Retract Reef's walkways by shrinking each thick walkway onto an amber spine you draw through its beacons, sliding every point along a straight segment without leaving the reef, tearing, or moving the spine.
levels.teaches: Thick shapes shrink to thin spines by sliding points along segments at constant speed (Hatcher's thick-letter example). A valid deformation retraction starts at the identity, ends inside A, never moves A, and is continuous. Rings and two-holed disks shrink to loops and graphs, never (by sliding) to a point.

beats.teach: A straight walkway with a given spine: scrub time t from 0 to 1 and watch each point slide along its segment; the four rules light up.
beats.practice: A thick T: draw a spine through all three beacons and run the slide.
beats.twist: A thick O (ring): a short spine fails — points must cross the hole and fall into the sea, or neighbors tear apart. Only a loop around the hole works.
beats.master: A disk with two holes (Hatcher's figure): find a spine that holds; Emmy notes the book shows three different ones. Then spot Count Null's four forged 'retractions', each breaking one rule.

levels.title: Bend, Don't Break
levels.concept: Homotopy of maps in general; homotopy rel A; retraction vs. deformation retraction (every space retracts to a point, but not every space deformation retracts to one).
levels.goal: Morph one map into another through a continuous family; keep a marked subspace still (rel A); catch the constant-map 'retraction' that isn't a deformation.

levels.title: Same Shape, Different Look
levels.concept: Homotopy equivalence (fg ≃ 1, gf ≃ 1), contractible spaces, mapping cylinders.
levels.goal: Show two walkway networks with different spines from 0-1 are 'the same shape' by building maps both ways and deforming the round trips back to the identity.

levels.title: Some Assembly Required
levels.concept: CW complexes: attach n-cells along their boundaries to the (n−1)-skeleton; S², torus, RP² from cells; Euler characteristic as a cell count.
levels.goal: Forge S², the torus (aba⁻¹b⁻¹) and RP² from vertices, edges and disks, previewing each attaching map before gluing.

levels.title: Cone Zone
levels.concept: Operations on spaces: products, quotients, cones, suspensions, wedges, joins — and the cells each inherits or adds.
levels.goal: Turn spaces into their cone, suspension and wedge with the Cell-Smith; build the torus again as S¹ × S¹ and match it to your 0-4 torus.

levels.title: Timber!
levels.concept: Collapsing a contractible subcomplex preserves homotopy type; collapse a spanning tree to turn any connected graph into a bouquet of circles; χ distinguishes bouquets.
levels.goal: Collapse only edges with distinct endpoints until each network is a bouquet; use Chi Euler's count to tell bouquets apart.

levels.title: Extension Cord
levels.concept: Bonus: the homotopy extension property; every CW pair has it.
levels.goal: Extend a prescribed motion of the boundary across a cylinder, cell by cell, without changing the start.

castle.title: The Hollow Throne
castle.outcome: Gyroid exposes three of Null's 'simplifications' as torn or illegal, but cannot refute his claim that a ring is secretly a point. Null escapes. The player now needs an invariant.

worlds.title: Bouquet Bastion
worlds.theme: Loop districts, ordered causeways and glass sheet-worlds. Loops are the weapon; the Commutator patrols.

null_claim.claim: The sphere is just as simple as a point — every loop on it shrinks.
null_claim.why_it_works_here: π₁(S²) = 0, so loops cannot see the sphere's hollow.

levels.title: Fixed Endpoints
levels.concept: Paths and path homotopy with endpoints held fixed; straight-line homotopy; homotopy classes; concatenation is well defined on classes.

levels.title: Loop de Loop
levels.concept: Based loops form the fundamental group: concatenation, constant loop, inverses; change of basepoint along a path.

levels.title: Winding Road
levels.concept: π₁(S¹) ≅ ℤ: lift loops to the helix ℝ → S¹; the lift's endpoint is the winding number, and homotopy cannot change it.

levels.title: No Way Out
levels.concept: Applications of π₁(S¹): no retraction D² → S¹, so every map D² → D² has a fixed point (Brouwer); fundamental theorem of algebra; Borsuk–Ulam in dimension 2.
levels.goal: Finally refute Count Null's World-0 claim: a ring is not a point, because its loop has winding number 1.

levels.title: Push It Forward
levels.concept: Induced homomorphisms f_*; retractions induce injections; π₁(X × Y) ≅ π₁(X) × π₁(Y), so π₁(torus) ≅ ℤ².

levels.title: Free Word Play
levels.concept: Free products: loops in a wedge of circles are reduced words; adjacent inverses cancel; different generators don't commute.

levels.title: Glue Job
levels.concept: Van Kampen's theorem; attaching a 2-cell kills its boundary word: π₁(torus) = ⟨a, b | aba⁻¹b⁻¹⟩, π₁(RP²) = ℤ₂, surfaces.

levels.title: Under Cover
levels.concept: Covering spaces; unique path and homotopy lifting; a loop's class lies in p_*π₁ exactly when its lift closes; sheets = index.

levels.title: Sheet Music
levels.concept: Classification: connected covers ↔ subgroups of π₁ (up to conjugacy); covers of S¹ ∨ S¹ as labeled graphs; universal covers (tree, plane).

levels.title: Deck the Halls
levels.concept: Deck transformations and group actions; normal covers; Sⁿ → RPⁿ.

levels.title: Free Agents
levels.concept: Bonus: graphs and free groups — subgroups of free groups are free, via covers of graphs.

levels.title: One Group to Rule
levels.concept: Bonus: K(G,1) spaces and graphs of groups.

castle.title: The Commutator's Keep
castle.outcome: The Commutator's patrol aba⁻¹b⁻¹ is nontrivial in the figure-eight (catch it with a cover where its lift doesn't close) but dies on the torus (the 2-cell). Null retreats to the sphere, where loops are blind.

worlds.title: Chain Delta
worlds.theme: Wetlands of oriented triangles where boundaries cancel and missing centers survive.

null_claim.claim: The torus and S¹ ∨ S¹ ∨ S² are the same place.

levels.title: Tile and Error
levels.concept: Δ-complexes: glue ordered simplices; torus, Klein bottle, RP² from two triangles.

levels.title: Boundary Issues
levels.concept: Simplicial chains, ∂∂ = 0, cycles modulo boundaries.

levels.title: Any Simplex Will Do
levels.concept: Singular homology and homotopy invariance.

levels.title: Chase Scene
levels.concept: Exact sequences, long exact sequence of a pair, diagram chasing.

levels.title: Cut and Paste
levels.concept: Excision and good pairs; H̃(X/A); homology of spheres.

levels.title: The Third Degree
levels.concept: Degree of sphere maps; antipodal map; hairy ball theorem.
levels.goal: Refute Null's World-1 claim: H₂(S²) ≅ ℤ sees the hollow that loops missed.

levels.title: Cell Block
levels.concept: Cellular homology from a CW structure; Euler characteristic revisited.

levels.title: Patchwork
levels.concept: Mayer–Vietoris sequences.

levels.title: Mod Squad
levels.concept: Homology with coefficients; ℤ₂ and nonorientable surfaces.

levels.title: Forget the Order
levels.concept: H₁ is π₁ made abelian; the Commutator's trick vanishes in homology.

levels.title: Classic Moves
levels.concept: Bonus: Jordan curve theorem, invariance of domain, division algebras.

levels.title: Fixed Ideas
levels.concept: Bonus: simplicial approximation and the Lefschetz fixed point theorem.

worlds.notes: 2.3 (axioms, categories and functors, pp. 160–165) is treated as lore between levels, not a level of its own.

castle.title: The Retractor
castle.outcome: Null's ball-to-boundary retractor B³ → S² is impossible because H₂(B³) = 0 — Brouwer again, one dimension up.

worlds.title: Cup Product Gardens
worlds.theme: Signal gardens where cochains read chains backwards and classes multiply.

null_claim.claim: Every map S³ → S² is trivial — homology sees nothing there.
null_claim.why_it_works_here: H̃_*(S³) and H̃_*(S²) live in different degrees, so homology gives no map to detect.

levels.title: Reverse Engineering
levels.concept: Cochains and coboundaries: dualize chains into a coefficient group G.

levels.title: Torsion Shift
levels.concept: Universal Coefficient Theorem: torsion appears one degree higher; cohomology of spaces.

levels.title: Front Face, Back Face
levels.concept: Cup product on simplices and the coboundary sign rule.

levels.title: A Cup of Counterexample
levels.concept: The cohomology ring distinguishes the torus from S¹ ∨ S¹ ∨ S².
levels.goal: Refute Null's World-2 claim with a nonzero cup product.

levels.title: Product Placement
levels.concept: Künneth formula for products.

levels.title: Polynomial Garden
levels.concept: RPⁿ and CPⁿ have truncated polynomial cohomology; Borsuk–Ulam.

levels.title: Which Way Is Up
levels.concept: Orientations; local homology; the orientation double cover.

levels.title: Both Sides of the Story
levels.concept: Poincaré duality: Hᵏ ≅ Hₙ₋ₖ for closed orientable manifolds; ℤ₂ otherwise.

levels.title: Perfect Pairing
levels.concept: Duality and cup product: the nondegenerate pairing (CP² vs. S² ∨ S⁴).

worlds.notes: Additional topics 3.A–3.H (pp. 261–336) are out of scope for the core path; candidates for secret levels.

castle.title: The Counterfeit Station
castle.outcome: The Commutator's disguise (matching homology, wrong ring) is unmasked. Null retreats up the tower into higher homotopy.

worlds.title: Postnikov Spire
worlds.theme: A tower whose rooms unfold into higher dimensions; the Null Crown sits at the top.

null_claim.claim: Give me the homotopy groups and I'll rebuild any space — the twists don't matter.
null_claim.why_it_works_here: Homotopy groups alone don't determine homotopy type; the k-invariants do the gluing.

levels.title: Cube Root
levels.concept: πₙ as cubes with boundary at the basepoint; πₙ is abelian for n ≥ 2 (slide subcubes past each other).

levels.title: Snap to Grid
levels.concept: Cellular approximation: πᵢ(Sⁿ) = 0 for i < n; CW approximation.

levels.title: Weak Spot
levels.concept: Whitehead's theorem: weak equivalences of CW complexes are homotopy equivalences.

levels.title: Suspension of Disbelief
levels.concept: Homotopy excision and Freudenthal suspension; πₙ(Sⁿ) ≅ ℤ via degree.

levels.title: One Group Per Floor
levels.concept: Eilenberg–MacLane spaces K(G, n).

levels.title: Hurewicz Hurrah
levels.concept: Hurewicz theorem: the first nonzero πₙ equals Hₙ.

levels.title: Hop Off
levels.concept: Fiber bundles and their long exact sequence; the Hopf fibration gives π₃(S²) ≅ ℤ.
levels.goal: Refute Null's World-3 claim: the Hopf map S³ → S² is essential.

levels.title: Stable Ground
levels.concept: Stable homotopy groups.

levels.title: Maps Are Classes
levels.concept: Cohomology as homotopy classes of maps to K(G, n).

levels.title: Fibration Station
levels.concept: Fibrations and the homotopy lifting property.

levels.title: A Twist in the Tower
levels.concept: Postnikov towers and k-invariants.

levels.title: Obstruction Course
levels.concept: Obstruction theory: extend maps cell by cell; the obstruction is a cohomology class.

worlds.notes: Additional topics 4.A–4.L (pp. 421–518) are out of scope for the core path; 4.B (Hopf invariant) is the best secret-level candidate.

castle.title: The Null Crown
castle.outcome: Gyroid rebuilds the Crown's tower stage by stage, installing the k-invariants Null threw away, and restores every province without erasing a single hole.

structure.model: Super Mario Bros. 3: chapter = world, key concept = level, a castle closes each world, bonus levels hold additional topics.
structure.level_beats: Every level runs teach → practice → twist → master.
recurrence: Count Null's claim in each world exploits the blind spot of the invariant the player has so far; the next world's tool refutes it (see each world's null_claim).
Field guide: the same spaces (circle, disk, sphere, torus, Klein bottle, RP², figure-eight, Möbius band, later CPⁿ) recur, and each world fills in a new column of invariants for them.
Tools persist like power-ups; levels list `prerequisites` (must have) and `reuses` (actively re-tested).
Castles are cumulative tests of the levels they list.
structure.page_note: Pages are topic start pages from contents.json plus the PDF text where checked; ranges are approximate until verified against the PDF.

superseded_levels.note: The concept agent's original 10-level plan, kept for reference; replaced by `worlds`.
